props.gloss_en: R' Shimon has muktze only for dried figs and raisins
the baraita: one who was eating figs [or grapes], left some, and took them up to the roof to make dried figs [raisins] may not eat them until he designates them
...and so you say of peaches, quinces and all other kinds of fruit
the fruit-on-the-roof baraita is R' Yehuda's
the fruit-on-the-roof baraita is R' Shimon's
once he took them up to the roof he put them out of his mind (so even one who was in the middle of eating needs designation)
R' Shimon son of Rabbi asks: unripe dates [set to ripen] -- are they muktze for R' Shimon?
Rabbi [answering by R' Shimon's limit] does not himself hold muktze -- the presumption the stam's question voices
the mishna: one may not water or slaughter desert animals [on Yom Tov]
...but one may water and slaughter domestic animals
the baraita: desert animals are those that go out at Passover and come in at the first rains
...domestic animals are those that go out to graze beyond the boundary and come back to sleep within it
Rabbi: both of those are domestic; desert animals are those that graze in the pasture and never enter the settlement, summer or winter

schemas.gloss_en: if R' Yehuda holds muktze where one did not push the thing away with his hands, then where he did, all the more so

frames.gloss_en: מני? אילימא רבי יהודה... אלא לאו רבי שמעון היא! -- whose is the fruit-on-the-roof baraita?
frames.exhaustive_gloss: the Gemara poses exactly two candidates (אילימא... אלא לאו...)

alternatives.gloss_en: attacked as redundant, then kept: לעולם רבי יהודה

eliminated_by.gloss_en: אילימא רבי יהודה -- ומה היכא דלא דחייה בידים אית ליה מוקצה, היכא דדחייה בידים לא כל שכן? (kv_dachyei_beyadayim): for R' Yehuda the baraita would teach nothing

rebuffed_by.gloss_en: לעולם רבי יהודה, ואוכל איצטריכא ליה: one might think that since he was in the middle of eating he needs no designation; it teaches that once he took them to the roof he put them out of mind (= p_heelan_lagag_asach_daato)

alternatives.gloss_en: the objector's conclusion (אלא לאו רבי שמעון היא), never eliminated -- the answer simply keeps R' Yehuda

objections.gloss_en: ומידי אחרינא לא? והתניא: ...and so you say of peaches, quinces and all other fruit -- and the baraita must be R' Shimon's (45a.7-8, frame f_teenim_mani)

answered_by.gloss_en: לעולם רבי יהודה, ואוכל איצטריכא ליה -- the baraita is R' Yehuda's and says nothing about R' Shimon (= p_teenim_kery; rebuff rb_ochel_itztrich)

objections.gloss_en: ורבי לית ליה מוקצה? והתנן: desert animals are not watered or slaughtered; ותניא: ...Rabbi says: desert animals are those that graze in the pasture and never come in -- so Rabbi does hold muktze for them

answered_by.gloss_en: איבעית אימא: הני נמי כגרוגרות וצימוקין דמיין -- these animals too are like dried figs and raisins
ואי בעית אימא: לדבריו דרבי שמעון קאמר ליה, וליה לא סבירא ליה -- he answered his son by R' Shimon's view and does not hold it himself

ואיבעית אימא: לדבריהם דרבנן קאמר להו -- I have no muktze at all; on your view, at least agree that those going out at Passover and coming in at the rains are domestic. ורבנן? אמרו ליה: לא, מדבריות נינהו
